# `silk/compress/brotli`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Decompress Brotli data (RFC 7932) in steps, with fixed memory and limits that you set.

## When to use
Use [`Brotli`](#Brotli) to read `.br` files or HTTP bodies with `Content-Encoding: br`. Make a decoder
with [`Brotli.make`](#Brotli.impl.make), and call [`Brotli.step`](#Brotli.impl.step) until it returns `Finished`. Call
[`Brotli.reset`](#Brotli.impl.reset) to decode another stream with the same storage. This module does not
compress.

## Details
The decoder supports all of RFC 7932: compressed, uncompressed, and metadata meta-blocks, all
context modes, and the static dictionary with its 121 word transforms. [`Brotli.make`](#Brotli.impl.make) allocates
all storage one time: the history window and the space for prefix code tables. [`Brotli.step`](#Brotli.impl.step)
does not allocate and keeps no borrow of your buffers, so you can move the decoder between
threads between calls.

A Brotli stream ends itself. The decoder returns `Finished` when the last meta-block is decoded
and all output is written, and it leaves the bytes after the stream unconsumed.

## Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` from [`Brotli.make`](#Brotli.impl.make) if the `Allocator` fails.
- [`BrotliError`](#BrotliError) if the configuration is not valid, the data is not valid, a limit is
  exceeded, or a call after the final input does not give exactly the input that is not consumed
  yet. `reason` gives the cause and `offset` the input position.

## Gotchas
The window holds `windowBytes` rounded down to a power of two. A stream can declare a larger
window than that and still decode, as long as no back-reference reaches further than the window
holds. A failure is permanent until [`Brotli.reset`](#Brotli.impl.reset).

## Examples
### Decode a short stream
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.compress.brotli { Brotli, BrotliError, BrotliLimits, BrotliProgress, BrotliStatus }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! BrotliError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut decoder = run Brotli.make(BrotliLimits.make())
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)

  // The reference encoder's output for "hi": one uncompressed meta-block and an empty last one.
  let input = b"\x8b\x00\x80hi\x03"
  let mut output: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  return match Brotli.step(&mut decoder, &input, &mut output, true) {
    Result<BrotliProgress, BrotliError>.Success { value } => {
      if value.status != BrotliStatus.Finished || value.written != 2 || output[0] != 104
        || output[1] != 105 {
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<BrotliProgress, BrotliError>.Failure {..} => 1
  }
}
```

Import as `Brotli` with `import silk.compress.brotli { Brotli }`.

## `BrotliLimits`

```silk
pub struct BrotliLimits
```

The resource limits for one stream. [`BrotliLimits.make`](#BrotliLimits.impl.make) gives defaults.

<a id="BrotliLimits.inputBytes"></a>

### Field `inputBytes`

```silk
pub inputBytes: u64
```

The maximum number of input bytes to consume.

<a id="BrotliLimits.outputBytes"></a>

### Field `outputBytes`

```silk
pub outputBytes: u64
```

The maximum number of decoded bytes.

<a id="BrotliLimits.windowBytes"></a>

### Field `windowBytes`

```silk
pub windowBytes: usize
```

The size of the history window that [`Brotli.make`](#Brotli.impl.make) allocates, rounded down to a power of two
and capped at 16 MiB, the largest window of the format. It must not be 0. A back-reference
further than the window fails with `WindowLimit`.

<a id="BrotliLimits.workspaceBytes"></a>

### Field `workspaceBytes`

```silk
pub workspaceBytes: usize
```

The storage budget other than the window: decoder state, context maps, and the space for the
prefix code tables of one meta-block. If it is too small for the fixed part, [`Brotli.make`](#Brotli.impl.make)
fails with `WorkspaceLimit`, and if a meta-block needs more table space than it leaves, the
step fails with `WorkspaceLimit`.

A decoding failure. It is permanent until [`Brotli.reset`](#Brotli.impl.reset).

Each later call returns the same `reason` and `offset` with no progress. The output that earlier

<a id="Brotli"></a>

## `Brotli`

```silk
pub struct Brotli
```

A Brotli decoder for one stream at a time. It owns all its storage.

### When to use
Use it to read `.br` files or HTTP bodies with `Content-Encoding: br`. Make a decoder with
[`Brotli.make`](#Brotli.impl.make), call [`Brotli.step`](#Brotli.impl.step) until it returns `Finished`, and call [`Brotli.reset`](#Brotli.impl.reset) to
decode another stream.

### Details
[`Brotli.make`](#Brotli.impl.make) allocates the window and the table space one time. [`Brotli.step`](#Brotli.impl.step) does not
allocate and keeps no borrow of your buffers, so you can move the decoder between threads
between calls.

### Gotchas
A failure is permanent until [`Brotli.reset`](#Brotli.impl.reset). Output that the stream wrote before a failure is
not valid.

<a id="Brotli.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Brotli`

```silk
impl Brotli
```

<a id="Brotli.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(limits: BrotliLimits) -> Self
    ! BrotliError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a decoder that uses `limits`, with storage from the ambient `Allocator`.

It allocates the window and the workspace. [`Brotli.step`](#Brotli.impl.step) does not allocate. Both come from
`Allocator.allocateZeroed`, so with the system allocator a large window takes memory only as
the stream fills it.

#### Errors
- [`BrotliError`](#BrotliError) with `WorkspaceLimit` if `workspaceBytes` is too small for the fixed state,
  or with `InvalidConfiguration` if `windowBytes` is 0. These checks come before the
  allocation.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="Brotli.impl.reset"></a>

### Method `reset`

```silk
pub fn reset(self: &mut Self) -> ()
```

Starts a new stream with the same limits and storage. It does not allocate. It drops the state
of the current stream and a failure.

<a id="Brotli.impl.step"></a>

### Method `step`

```silk
pub fn step(self: &mut Self, input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8], finalInput: bool) -> Result<
    BrotliProgress,
    BrotliError,
  >
```

Decodes from `input` into `output` and returns how much it consumed and wrote.

On the next call, give only the input after the consumed prefix, and use only the written
prefix of the output. Set `finalInput` when `input` holds all remaining data. After that, each
call must set `finalInput` and give exactly the input that is not consumed yet. `NeedOutput`
with an empty output makes no progress. After `Finished`, each call returns `Finished` and
consumes nothing.

#### Errors
- [`BrotliError`](#BrotliError) if the data is not valid, a [`BrotliLimits`](#BrotliLimits) value would be exceeded, the
  final input ends early (`Truncated`), or the call changes the final input (`InvalidState`).

#### Gotchas
A failure is permanent until [`Brotli.reset`](#Brotli.impl.reset).
